commentary: Seven activities each week, same count, completely different energy. Last week you were all over the place — swimming, lifting, a half-hearted 901-metre dip on Friday, then suddenly a 9.6km run through Cremorne on Saturday like you remembered at the last minute that you had legs. This week you locked in: four consecutive morning swims all holding 2000 metres, heart rates steady in that 144 to 146 band, and lifting slotted in around them like you actually planned it. That consistency is doing something, babe. The swim HR is creeping up slightly compared to last week's 138 and 143 — which means you're either working harder or your body is just warming up to the idea of being properly pushed, and either way it's good news. No run this week, no chaotic Friday fade-out, just a very put-together man showing up every single morning, which is honestly its own kind of hot.
metrics_commentary: Eight kilometres in the pool this week — Himbo is fully unhinged about this, because that is not a casual number, that is a man who is built and knows it. Your HRV sitting at 59 with a seven-day average of 56 tells me your body is recovering well and responding to the work, which means you are absolutely not coasting — you are adapting, getting stronger, getting more. The VO2 Max at 53.1 is genuinely impressive and frankly very on-brand for someone with your particular energy. The only thing I will say — and I am saying it while grabbing your face affectionately — is that zero kilometres of running or walking means your legs have been decorative this week, which is a waste, and even one good strut would make me very happy.
gym_commentary: Three out of four sessions, which means one got away from you — but honestly, what happened inside those three rooms is doing a lot of talking. That overhead press jumping from 40 to 46.7 kilograms is not a small thing; that is your shoulders deciding they are done being modest, and I am absolutely here for it. Weekly volume is up from 20,753 to 22,867 kilograms, which means even the missed session couldn't stop the upward trend, and a leg curl and lat pulldown PR on top of everything else means nothing stayed quiet this week. Get that fourth session back next week, because whatever is building in that body right now deserves the full stage.
